en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Waki narrated to us. (And via another chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Ubad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swearing that {These are two opponents} was revealed, like the hadith of Hushaym.

Amr ibn Zurara narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Ubad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swearing an oath that: {These are two opponents who disputed concerning their Lord} (Quran 22:19), it was revealed concerning those who duelled on the Day of Badr: Hamza, Ali, and Ubayda ibn al-Harith, and Utba and Shayba the two sons of Rabiah, and al-Walid ibn Utba.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to us. (And via another chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us, both from Abu Hayyan with this chain of narration, similar to their hadith, except that Ibn Ulayyah mentioned grapes in his hadith, as Ibn Idris said, and in the hadith of Isa he mentioned raisins, as Ibn Mushir said.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Idris informed us: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn Umar, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: To proceed: O people, the prohibition of wine was revealed when it was made from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley; and wine is whatever clouds the mind. And three things, O people, I wished that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) had clarified for us with a covenant upon which we could rely: the inheritance of the grandfather, the kalalah (one who dies leaving neither parent nor child), and certain categories from the chapters of usury.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn Umar, who said: Umar delivered a sermon from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). He praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said: To proceed: Beware, wine was prohibited on the day it was prohibited when it was produced from five things: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and honey; and wine is whatever clouds the mind. And there are three things, O people, I wished that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) had clarified for us: the inheritance of the grandfather, the kalalah, and certain categories from the chapters of usury.

Abdullah ibn Muti narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Surah at-Tawbah? He said: At-Tawbah? Rather, it is the Exposome (al-Fadihah). It continued to be revealed with: 'And among them...', 'And among them...', until they thought that none of us would be left unmentioned in it. I said: Surah al-Anfal? He said: That is Surah Badr. I said: Surah al-Hashr? He said: It was revealed concerning Banu an-Nadir.

Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Husayn narrated to us, from Qatada, from Abdullah ibn Ma'bad az-Zimmani, from Abdullah ibn Utba, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud regarding: {Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord} (Quran 17:57). He said: It was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of jinn. The jinn embraced Islam, while the humans who used to worship them were unaware, so there was revealed: {Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord} (Quran 17:57).

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi al-Abdi narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abdullah regarding: {Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord} (Quran 17:57). He said: A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn, and that group of jinn embraced Islam, while the humans clung to worshipping them, so there was revealed: {Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord} (Quran 17:57). And Bishr ibn Khalid narrated it to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us, from Shu'ba, from Sulayman with this chain of narration.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abdullah concerning the saying of the Almighty: {Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord, which of them will be nearest} (Quran 17:57). He said: A group of jinn had embraced Islam while they were being worshipped, but those who used to worship them persisted in their worship even though that group of jinn had embraced Islam.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to me: Abu Awana narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir that Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave-girl named Musaykah and another named Umaymah, and he used to compel them to fornication. They complained about that to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and so Allah revealed: {And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution} up to His saying: {Forgiving and Merciful} (Quran 24:33).

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us from Abu Muawiya—and the wording is that of Abu Kurayb—Abu Muawiya narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul used to say to a slave-girl of his: 'Go and earn something for us through prostitution.' So Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed: {And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity, in order that you may seek the temporary gain of worldly life. And whoever compels them, then indeed, after their compulsion, Allah is}—to them—{Forgiving and Merciful} (Quran 24:33).

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. (And via another chain) Abu Bakr ibn Nafi narrated to me—and the wording is his—Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A woman used to circumambulate the House while naked, saying: 'Who will lend me a waist-wrap to put over her private part?' And she would say: 'Today some of it or all of it may appear, but whatever appears of it, I do not make lawful.' So this verse was revealed: {Take your adornment at every masjid} (Quran 7:31).

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la as-Sadafi narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Awn ibn Abdullah, from his father, that Ibn Mas'ud said: There was no more than four years between our embracing Islam and Allah admonishing us with this verse: {Has the time not come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of Allah} (Quran 57:16).

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'ba. (And via another chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara saying: When the Ansar performed Hajj and returned, they would not enter houses except from their backs. He said: A man from the Ansar came and entered through his front door, and he was reproached for that. So this verse was revealed: {And it is not righteousness that you enter houses from the back} (Quran 2:189).

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ahmad ibn Abdah ad-Dabbi narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn Abi Shayba; he said: narrated to us, while the other two said: informed us—Sufyan, from Amr, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some Muslims encountered a man with a small flock of sheep of his, and he said: 'Peace be upon you (as-salamu alaykum).' They seized him and killed him, and took that flock of sheep. So there was revealed: {And do not say to the one who gives you a greeting of peace: You are not a believer} (Quran 4:94). And Ibn Abbas recited it as 'as-salam'.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abu Muawiya informed us: Abu Umays narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it, and he said: 'the last Surah,' and he said 'Abd al-Majid' without saying 'Ibn Suhayl'.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, Harun ibn Abdullah, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Abd said: informed us, while the other two said: narrated to us—Ja'far ibn Awn: Abu Umays informed us, from Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utba, who said: Ibn Abbas said to me: 'Do you know'—and Harun said: 'Do you know'—'the last Surah of the Quran that was revealed entirely?' I said: Yes, {When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest} (Quran 110:1). He said: You have spoken the truth. And in the narration of Ibn Abi Shayba: 'Do you know which Surah...', and he did not say 'the last'.

Abdullah ibn Hashim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr al-Abdi narrated to me, both saying: Yahya—and he is Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Is there any repentance for one who kills a believer intentionally? He said: No. He said: So I recited to him this verse which is in al-Furqan: {And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right} (Quran 25:68) to the end of the verse. He said: This is a Meccan verse that was abrogated by a Medinan verse: {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally} (Quran 4:93). And in the narration of Ibn Hashim: 'So I recited this verse which is in al-Furqan: {Except him who repents}.'

Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Abu an-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Laythi narrated to us: Abu Muawiya—meaning Shayban—narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed in Mecca: {And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity} (Quran 25:68) up to His saying: {in humiliation} (Quran 25:69). Then the polytheists said: 'What benefit will Islam be to us when we have ascribed equals to Allah, killed the soul that Allah has forbidden, and committed abominations?' So Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed: {Except him who repents, believes, and does righteous work} (Quran 25:70) to the end of the verse. He said: As for the one who entered Islam and understood it, and then killed, there is no repentance for him.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza instructed me to ask Ibn Abbas about these two verses: {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally} (Quran 4:93). So I asked him and he said: Nothing has abrogated it. And regarding this verse: {And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right} (Quran 25:68), he said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism (shirk).

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. (And via another chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: an-Nadr informed us, both saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, with this chain of narration. In the hadith of Ibn Ja'far: 'It was revealed among the last of what was revealed.' And in the hadith of an-Nadr: 'It is indeed among the last of what was revealed.'

Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn an-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The people of Kufa differed concerning this verse: {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell} (Quran 4:93). So I traveled to Ibn Abbas and asked him about it, and he said: It was revealed among the last of what was revealed, and then nothing abrogated it.
And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated it to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Muawiya informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, who said: Aisha said to me: O son of my sister, they were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him), but instead they reviled them.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, regarding the saying of the Mighty and Sublime: {And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion} (Quran 4:128). She said: It was revealed concerning a woman who is married to a man, and perhaps he is no longer inclined to have much to do with her, yet she has companionship and children with him, so she dislikes that he should separate from her and says to him: 'You are released from obligation regarding my share.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, regarding the verse: {And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion} (Quran 4:128). She said: It was revealed concerning a woman who is married to a man and her companionship with him has been long, and he wishes to divorce her, so she says: 'Do not divorce me; keep me, and you are released from obligation regarding me.' So this verse was revealed.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, regarding the saying of the Mighty and Sublime: {When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted in terror and hearts reached the throats} (Quran 33:10). She said: That was on the Day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).
And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of narration.

And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha, regarding the saying of the Exalted: {And whoever is rich should refrain, and whoever is poor should consume in what is reasonable} (Quran 4:6). She said: It was revealed concerning the guardian of an orphan: that he may take from his wealth if he is in need, according to his work and in what is reasonable.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, regarding His saying: {and whoever is poor should consume in what is reasonable} (Quran 4:6). She said: It was revealed concerning the manager of an orphan's wealth who maintains it and tends to it: that if he is in need, he may consume from it.
